summary: Ran the molecular tests for M1-S05 (docs, metadata-builder) of build tier2-webhook: both always-on checks and the step's four declared acceptance tests. xml parsed the step's one file cleanly. The manifest check spanned artefacts/M1-S01 through M1-S04 (M1-S05 itself carries no component files, only package.xml and deploy-order.md) and found 33 derived members bidirectionally consistent with the 33 members in artefacts/M1-S05/package.xml - no member without a file, no file without a member - with TestDataFactory's two source copies (M1-S03, M1-S04) verified byte-identical by SHA-256 to each other and to templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls, so the single manifest member is correct rather than a missed duplicate. The declared checker (check_deployment_manifest.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S05) exited 0 with exactly the two WARN findings the plan predicted (ExternalCredential, NamedCredential), and check-outputs reported ok:true. The manual test (deploy-order read at the M1 gate) is tickable - it names a concrete, checkable outcome even though it is not literal Given/When/Then - and is deferred to skipped_manual[] verbatim. Status set to tested.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 HIGH: every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed over the full cross-step scope the step's own test description requires, and every result (checker exit code, check-outputs JSON, xml parse, manifest derivation) came from an exit code or a parse this agent observed directly rather than from the prior envelopes' claims - the TestDataFactory byte-identity and the 33/33 member count were independently re-derived and re-hashed, not taken on trust.

inputs_received.precondition_status: built (verified in plan.json before any test ran)

process_observations.observation: The declared checker's exit code and finding set matched the step's own acceptance-test description exactly - exit 0, exactly two WARN (ExternalCredential, NamedCredential), zero blocking - on the first run, with no repair pass needed.

The build-wide manifest two-way check was independently re-derived from the file tree under artefacts/M1-S01..S04 (not copied from the metadata-builder envelope's member_counts), and it agrees with that envelope exactly: 33 manifest members, 33 derived members, 0 missing in either direction.

TestDataFactory's byte-identity across M1-S03, M1-S04, and templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls was independently re-hashed (SHA-256) rather than accepted from the metadata-builder envelope's claim, and matched: 2f87c8c3...de782c for both .cls, a242f6e2...8ddea32 for both .cls-meta.xml.

The AuthHeader clause inside steps[M1-S05].inputs.manual_steps_the_deploy_does_not_perform (item 1) is pre-amendment prose - it reads as a single fully-resolvable manual confirmation, while artefacts/M1-S05/deploy-order.md section 3 step 1 already documents the narrower, corrected reading (grammar-parses-on-deploy plus a separate UAT confirmation) under decision D-M1S02-06 / finding PV-007. This is the same prose lag the metadata-builder and build-step-runner envelopes both flagged; it is reported again here because it sits inside the manual test this agent classified, not because it is new.

The declared manual test's expected text ('confirming the AuthHeader formula grammar, entering the API key...') is phrased as a checklist read rather than literal Given/When/Then, so it was checked against the testability bar (a boolean, observable outcome) rather than against Gherkin form for its pass/fail classification. It clears that bar - a reviewer can tick each of the five named items against deploy-order.md - but a human should confirm whether the shorthand 'confirming the AuthHeader formula grammar' is meant to already carry the D-M1S02-06 narrowing or is a stale summary of the original single-step framing; this agent does not resolve that judgment call.
M1-S05 is now tested and is the last step of M1; every other step is documented.
process_observations.followup_reason: M1-S05 needs its documentation pass, including recording the plan-text divergences (inputs.members.ApexClass count, inputs.deploy_order sequencing, the AuthHeader prose lag) in decisions.md, before the M1 milestone can be verified.
